metadata.title: Metagraph Encodings over Identified Triples: Exact Images, Temporal Integrity, and Structural Depth
metadata.description:
Identified triples give statements identities that other statements can reference, so set-valued incidence, higher-order endpoints and containment fit on one carrier. We argue that this representation is cheap and that invertibility is a separate integrity obligation, and we state that obligation exactly.

For finite directed hypergraphs, nonempty-end Basu–Blanning metagraphs, identified higher-order metagraphs, a well-founded ubergraph fragment and a finite attributed annotating presentation, we give source signatures and exact image constraints under which encoding and decoding are inverse up to renaming, and we show that each constraint is necessary.

Four results go beyond roundtrips: (1) a snapshot theorem that separates asserted rows from retained referents, so an annotation may be valid outside its bearer's interval; (2) a supersession relation that records identity across versions; (3) an executable-metapath recognizer that decides in linear time whether an edge set can fire, with a characterization of when it agrees with walk reachability; (4) operational consumers for reference rank, namely bulk-load strata and retraction-cascade depth.

Evidence: exhaustive bounded enumeration, seeded randomized property tests, SHACL/SPARQL validators tested for agreement with a Python checker, and a Lean 4 proof of the directed roundtrip under canonical naming. No performance or retrieval results are reported. Source code, checkers, validators and the Lean proof: https://github.com/Volland/tiramemsu (paper/metagraphs-from-identified-triples/). Revision 2, 5 October 2026. Companion to “Layered Bitemporal Graphs” (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23139228).
